label: t3-lumen-deep
topic: Track 3 deep literature: MDCK cyst lumen shape (Vasquez et al 2021) and the physics of lumen geometry
summary:
STATE OF THE ART, MDCK CYST LUMEN SHAPE (Track 3). Written 2026-11-12; 21 distinct papers cited (plus the published DOI of one preprint and the bioRxiv version of another); 13 were read in full text (two only in the sections searched) and 8 as abstract only, as stated per paper in citations.how_verified.

GROUND-UP EXPLANATION (each step tagged M measured, D derived, A assumed)
1. A lumen is the fluid-filled hollow inside a ring or ball of epithelial cells. MDCK (dog kidney) cells grown in Matrigel form such balls ('cysts' or 'spheroids') with one lumen within about a day. [M: Vasquez 2021]
2. Each cell becomes polarised: one face (apical) faces the lumen, the opposite (basal) faces the gel, the sides (lateral) touch neighbours. The apical face is built by delivering membrane and polarity proteins (PTEN/PIP2, Cdc42, aPKC, Rab11a-Rab8a-exocyst, an AMIS site). [M: Martin-Belmonte 2007, Bryant 2010]
3. The apical faces are non-sticky (the two sides of a young lumen sit 200-300 nm apart), so a gap stays open. [M for the gap; A that non-adhesion is the cause]
4. Classical physics view: if cells pump salt and water into the gap, the fluid pushes outward with pressure P. A skin with tension T enclosing pressure P obeys Young-Laplace, P = T x (sum of the two curvatures); for a sphere of radius R, P = 2T/R. [D: textbook law; A: uniform tension, single P] A pressurised lumen should therefore be convex everywhere. [D]
5. Measurement: MDCK lumens are not round. Sphericity (1 is a perfect sphere) is 0.3-0.7 and 13-48 percent of the lumen surface is concave (bowed into the lumen) while the outer cyst surface stays almost spherical. [M: Vasquez; own recomputation n=35] A single-pressure, uniform-tension lumen cannot do that. [D]
6. Perturbations: making the junctions leaky (claudin knockout) should lose pressure yet shape is unchanged; drugs that change fluid pumping or acutely wreck the cytoskeleton change lumen shape little by the authors' reading. [M] Their conclusion is that apical area per cell, regulated by trafficking, dominates shape while pressure only adds roundness. [D, model-based]
7. Their model: a 2D vertex model (cells as polygons) with a preferred apical length l_a, a preferred basal length, a stringency k and a lumen-area/pressure term; run from 3 to 10 cells. Larger l_a lowers solidity at low pressure; pressure raises it; solidity rises with size even at zero pressure. [D] Pressure is dimensionless there and never measured in those cysts. [M: absence verified]
8. Counter-evidence and refinements: an independent lab measures 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and sees lumen number/fusion governed by pressure [M: Lu 2025]; Mukenhirn 2024 and Guha Ray 2026 show tight junctions control lumen opening/buckling through pressure-tension balance, with lateral and basal tensions also modulated [M, abstract-level]. Mouse blastocyst and zebrafish ear are the strongly pressure-driven cases (hundreds of Pa) [M].
9. Laws in the library (law set 1.8.1): only the thin-wall Laplace bound (physiology-laplace) applies; it needs a wall strength and thickness no one has supplied here. The richer Young-Laplace / Plateau theorems live only in the older leanbio tree. [library fact]

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED WITH NUMBERS: lumen sphericity 0.3-0.7; concave fraction 13-48 percent (own, n=35); WT/qKO solidity 0.865 vs 0.893 (p=0.88); pressure 65 Pa MDCK cysts (n=27), 100-300 Pa zebrafish ear; MDCK dome tension 1-2 mN/m.
WHAT IS CONTESTED: (a) role of pressure (Vasquez no; Lu, Mukenhirn yes, in different conditions/sizes); (b) whether Rab11a lowers solidity at matched size (paper yes; my simple tests find no significant difference, unconfirmed); (c) whether ddAVP changes shape (paper modest; day-3 medians 0.552 vs 0.881 in the source table, size-confounded); (d) constancy of apical length per cell (paper/Guha Ray constant; own l_a vs N rho 0.01, -0.44, +0.61 across genotypes; lumen area per cell CV 0.50); (e) tension scale (Lu model 0.1 mN/m vs dome 1-2 mN/m).
KEY EXPERIMENTS/MODELS IN ORDER: 2007 PTEN-PIP2-Cdc42 apical identity; 2008 Cdc42 spindle orientation (Caco-2); 2010 Rab11a-Rabin8-Rab8a AMIS; 2012 confinement; 2013 Cerruti non-equilibrium multilumen model; 2014/2017 vertex-model reviews; 2017 Ruiz-Herrero hydraulic oscillations; 2018 Dasgupta lumen growth physics and Latorre superelasticity; 2019 Chan, Dumortier, Mosaliganti hydraulics; 2021 Vasquez geometry model and Le Verge-Serandour coarsening theory, Torres-Sanchez review; 2023 Bebelman bulkheads; 2024 Mukenhirn tight junctions; 2025-26 Lu (65 Pa) and Guha Ray (3D vertex model).
BEST REVIEWS: Torres-Sanchez/Kerr Winter/Salbreux 2021 (tissue hydraulics); Navis and Bagnat 2015; Fletcher et al. 2014 and Alt et al. 2017 (vertex models).
OPEN PROBLEMS: how apical area is set and why it follows a per-cell constant; 3D rather than 2D vertex models matched to the same cysts; a joint dataset with pressure, tension and 3D shape in the same cyst; reconciling the 0.1 vs 1-2 mN/m tension scales; mapping dimensionless p to pascals; why the model sweep does not beat a constant on WT solidity (earlier design pilot, not re-run by me).
lay_summary: Many organs are made of tubes and sacs with a hollow space inside, called a lumen. Kidney-cell clumps grown in the lab make such a hollow, and you might expect it to be round like a water balloon, because fluid pressure pushes evenly on the wall. Measurements show it is not round: up to about half of its inner surface dents inwards, like a half-deflated beach ball. A 2021 study argued that the shape is set mainly by how much inner-facing skin each cell makes and by how many cells there are, with pressure adding only some roundness. Other labs measured a real pressure of about 65 pascals in these clumps and say pressure matters more, so the question is still open. The numbers I recomputed from the published tables agree with the dents but do not confirm every claim in the paper.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] MDCK cells embedded in Matrigel spontaneously form hollow spheroids within 24 h; at 18-24 h the two opposing apical cortices of a young lumen are 200-300 nm apart by lattice light-sheet imaging. The authors infer apical surfaces are intrinsically non-adhesive (an inference, not measured).
findings.evidence_quote: MDCK cells spontaneously form hollow spheroids within 24 h

findings.claim: [MEASURED] A positive luminal pressure with uniform surface tension should give convex (outward-bowed) lumen walls; Vasquez et al. state this as the premise they test, citing blastocyst and bile canaliculus as cases where convex curvature is documented.
findings.evidence_quote: Importantly, a positive luminal pressure should produce convex lumen surfaces that bow outwards toward the surrounding cells.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Lumens of 35 MDCK spheroids (7-30 cells in the intermediate set) are irregular: sphericity runs from about 0.70 down to about 0.3, less spherical than a cube (0.81).
findings.value: 0.3-0.70 (paper); own recomputation median 0.484, min 0.276, max 0.712, n=35
findings.evidence_quote: The sphericity of lumens ranged from Ψ ~ 0.70 to very far from spherical ( Ψ ~ 0.3)

findings.claim: [MEASURED] The fraction of lumen surface with negative (concave) mean curvature is 10 percent to over 50 percent in the paper; the basal (outer) surface is almost fully convex. My recomputation from the per-cyst table gives 13.3 to 48.1 percent (median 33.8) for the lumen and median 11.4 percent for the whole-cyst surface, a small disagreement with the paper wording.
findings.evidence_quote: The percent of the total lumen surface area with negative mean curvature varied from 10% to over 50%

findings.claim: [MEASURED] The outer (basal) cyst surface is nearly spherical while the lumen is not, so the irregularity belongs to the lumen. Own check: whole-cyst sphericity median 0.732, min 0.615.
findings.evidence_quote: the sphericity and percent concavity of the basal surfaces of the spheroids were close to 1 and 0%, respectively

findings.claim: [MEASURED, own] Sphericity formula check: recomputing psi = pi^(1/3)(6V)^(2/3)/A from the file columns vol_lumen and SA_lumen reproduces spher_lumen to within 0.0000 (max abs diff).

The paper describes an abrupt size-dependent crossover to sphericity about 0.7 at radius about 10 um; the 3D data behind it are thin (3 points).

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Pressure-pharmacology: ddAVP (fluid secretion up) and ouabain (Na/K-ATPase inhibitor) did not strongly change 2D lumen solidity for lumens of about four to tens of cells, in the authors reading.
findings.evidence_quote: for lumens of approximately four to tens of cells, modulating fluid pumping via ddAVP or ouabain did not strongly influence lumen shape

findings.claim: [MEASURED, own] That reading is size-dependent. At day 3 the median solidity is 0.881 (control, n=23), 0.552 (ddAVP, n=20), 0.881 (ouabain, n=19); at day 7 all three are 0.989-0.996. A crude linear size adjustment (solidity ~ normalised radius + treated) gives treated minus control of -0.255 (p=0.0013) for ddAVP and -0.247 (p=0.0042) for ouabain at day 3, but solidity vs size is a sharp step, not a line, so this adjustment is only a flag, not a test. The paper used a 2D Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, which I did not run.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Claudin quintuple knockout (leaky tight junctions) cysts have lumen solidity not significantly different from wild type, and lumens as large or larger. Own check: WT median 0.865 (n=53) vs Cldn-qKO 0.893 (n=25), Mann-Whitney p=0.881.
findings.evidence_quote: Cldn-qKO cells formed lumens whose solidity did not differ from wildtype to a significant degree

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Acute cytoskeleton ablation (latrunculin A, ML-7, Y-27632, nocodazole) did not significantly change lumen volume, surface area or solidity over 18 min (n=8 DMSO, 11 inhibitors).
findings.evidence_quote: Thus, the size and overall shape of lumens were both robust to an acute and dramatic perturbation to the cytoskeleton.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Rab11a-GFP overexpression (n=51) is reported to enlarge the apical domain and lower solidity at equal cell number. Own check does NOT reproduce a difference by simple methods: overall medians WT 0.865 (n=53) vs Rab11a 0.895 (n=51), Mann-Whitney p=0.755; solidity ~ normalised radius + Rab11a gives -0.046 (se 0.025, p=0.066, n=104). Rab11a lumens are larger (median normalised radius 0.995 vs 0.574), so the claim rests on a size-matched 2D KS test I could not run. Mark as unconfirmed by my method.
findings.evidence_quote: Rab11a-GFP spheroids generated a significantly larger apical domain and a significantly decreased solidity, compared to wildtype cells with the same number of cells

findings.claim: [MEASURED, own] Measured apical length per cell l_a (dimensionless, Fig 6 sheet): WT mean 0.754 (n=53), Rab11a-GFP 0.879 (n=51), Cldn-qKO 1.007 (n=25). Within genotype, Spearman(l_a, cell number) is 0.01 (WT, n=52), -0.44 (Rab11a, n=51), +0.61 (Cldn-qKO, n=25): apical length per cell is size-independent in WT but not in the two perturbed genotypes.

findings.claim: [ASSUMED/DERIVED] Vasquez model: 2D vertex model of N cells (each a curved basal side, two straight lateral sides, a curved apical side), energy terms for preferred apical length l_a, preferred basal length l_b, lateral length 0, stringency k, and a lumen-area (pressure) term p. Grown from 3 to 10 cells. k is explicitly not cortical tension.
findings.evidence_quote: Spheroids were simulated as they grew from 3 to 10 cells in size for each set of parameters.

findings.claim: [ASSUMED] The model is 2D, treats apical and basolateral properties as identical across cells, and does not say how apical size is regulated.
findings.evidence_quote: it models a two-dimensional cross-section of a three-dimensional object

findings.claim: [DERIVED] In the model, higher pressure raises solidity at a given cell number; larger preferred apical length lowers solidity at low pressure; solidity still rises with cell number even at zero pressure.
findings.evidence_quote: lumens tended to have higher solidity with cell number and increasing size even if luminal pressure was zero

findings.claim: [ASSUMED] For Cldn-qKO the model sets l_a to 1.0 and divides p by ten, justified by measured permeability, and reports only a modest effect on solidity but a rise in basal length and lumen area. The factor ten is a fitting constraint, not a measured pressure.
findings.evidence_quote: increasing l a to 1.0 (Fig. 6a ) and decreasing p by ten-fold, as expected from measurements of epithelial permeability

findings.claim: [MEASURED, own] The published model sweep (Fig 5 source data) has 15,030 rows over n_cells 3-10, l_a 12 values, l_l 7 values, l_b 9 values, P 14 values, k 12 values (sha256 f06ddb26...46140). Pressure is dimensionless; no pascal value appears anywhere in the Vasquez text (searched for digit + Pa).

findings.claim: [DERIVED, own] Dimensional bridge: for a sphere Laplace gives R = 2T/P. With P = 65 Pa (Lu 2025) and sheet tension 1 mN/m (Latorre 2018 MDCK domes) R = 30.8 um; with 2 mN/m R = 61.5 um; with Lu's model value gamma = 100 Pa um = 0.1 mN/m, R = 3.1 um. The factor 10-20 between the two tension scales is unresolved here (different quantities or conditions; not checked).
findings.source: own calculation: analyse_vq.py last block (arithmetic 2*1e-3/65 = 3.08e-5 m for T=1 mN/m)

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Apical surface and lumen generation is organised by PTEN-driven apical PtdIns(4,5)P2, Anx2, Cdc42 and aPKC in 3D MDCK culture; loss of any of PTEN, Anx2, Cdc42 or aPKC prevents normal apical surface and lumen development.
findings.evidence_quote: PTEN localizes to the apical plasma membrane during epithelial morphogenesis to mediate the enrichment of PtdIns(4,5)P2 at this domain

findings.claim: [MEASURED] A Rab11a-Rabin8-Rab8a-exocyst network directs Cdc42-dependent apical exocytosis; components assemble at a transient apical membrane initiation site (AMIS) to form the lumen.
findings.evidence_quote: Rab11a regulates apical traffic and lumen formation via the Rab GEF Rabin8, and its target Rab8a.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Spindle orientation places the apical domain: in Caco-2 cysts (not MDCK) the apical domain stays at the centre by spindle orientation and asymmetric abscission; 91 percent of midbodies are central in control multicellular structures, and Cdc42 depletion mis-positions apical surfaces.
findings.evidence_quote: 91% of midbodies are located in the center of the developing cyst

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Cell confinement on micropatterns (700 vs 1,600 um^2 adhesion area) raises lumen-formation efficiency by limiting peripheral actin contractility and favouring centrosome positioning after the first division.
findings.evidence_quote: cell confinement, by controlling cell spreading, limits peripheral actin contractility and promotes centrosome positioning and lumen initiation after the first cell division

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Multilumen cysts arise from fast, out-of-equilibrium growth even with correct spindle orientation; slowing division with aphidicolin partially rescues the multilumen phenotype in aPKC-inhibited cysts.
findings.evidence_quote: The occurrence of an aberrant multilumen phenotype was linked to fast nonequilibrium growth, even when geometric control of cell division was correctly enforced.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Independent lab: MDCK cysts have hydrostatic pressure about 65 Pa (mean, n=27 cysts, 3 experiments) vs about 0 Pa in epiblast models (n=22), from laser-cut outflow via Hagen-Poiseuille.
findings.evidence_quote: Hydrostatic pressure measurements show an average of 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and close to 0 Pa in epiblasts.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Starting from controlled initial cell numbers, MDCK lumen number rises with initial cell number (peak 1 lumen for 1 cell at 24 h to 6 for 16 cells), all cysts end near a single lumen, and neighbouring lumens fuse by breaking junctions over about 60 h.
findings.evidence_quote: ranging from a peak of 1 lumen for 1 initial cell at 24 h to 6 lumens on average for 16 initial cells

findings.claim: [DERIVED, by Lu et al. model] Without pressure (dp near 0 Pa) a lumen needs about 10 cells to nucleate; with large dp two cells nucleate one. Model parameters gamma_A = gamma_L = 100 Pa um, R0 = 20 um.
findings.evidence_quote: When Δp is close to 0 Pa, lumen formation requires a minimum threshold of 10 cells to nucleate a lumen.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Tight-junction work (Dev Cell 2024): claudin barrier not needed for hydraulic inflation; ZO scaffold loss gives lumen collapse and apical folding; tight junctions lower cortical tension via myosin inhibition; excess apical area helps lumen opening. Full text not accessible, abstract only; numeric pressures and tensions not read.
findings.evidence_quote: the depletion of the zonula occludens scaffold resulted in lumen collapse and folding of apical membranes

findings.claim: [MEASURED, from abstract] Same paper: excess apical area contributes to lumen opening, which links back to the Vasquez apical-area picture.
findings.evidence_quote: our results suggest that excess apical area contributes to lumen opening

findings.claim: [DERIVED/MEASURED] Follow-up (PRX Life 2026): a mean-field 3D vertex model with lateral and basal tensions reproduces the ZO-KO shape instability quantitatively; cysts respond by modulating lateral and basal tensions, not only pressure and apical belt tension. Single-cell apical area is reported constant in WT, ZO-KO and CLDN-KO by linear fits (figure; values not read).
findings.evidence_quote: We develop a mean-field three-dimensional vertex model of these cysts that reproduces the experimental shape instability quantitatively.

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Mouse blastocyst contrast case: lumenal pressure doubles during development; tension past a critical threshold ruptures the trophectoderm and the blastocyst collapses. Abstract only; no numbers read.
findings.evidence_quote: there is a twofold increase in lumenal pressure during blastocyst development

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Blastocyst lumen positioning: pressurised fluid fractures cell-cell contacts into hundreds of micrometre-size lumens that coarsen into one (Ostwald-like).
findings.evidence_quote: accumulation of pressurized fluid fractures cell-cell contacts into hundreds of micrometer-size lumens

findings.claim: [DERIVED] Hydro-osmotic coarsening model: lumen number falls with a dynamic scaling law N(t) ~ t^(-2/5) in the pure hydraulic regime; ion pumping prevents collective collapse and changes the law.
findings.evidence_quote: we generically observe a coarsening behavior characterized by a dynamic scaling law

findings.claim: [DERIVED] Physics of lumen growth: balance of osmotic pumping and paracellular leak predicts a critical pumping threshold for stable lumen expansion.
findings.evidence_quote: Our model predicts a critical pumping threshold to expand stable lumens.

findings.claim: [DERIVED, theory plus experiment] A soft permeable spherical shell relieves pressure by bursting, shrinking and regrowing: hydraulically gated size oscillations.
findings.evidence_quote: these shells can relieve internal pressure by bursting intermittently, shrinking and re-growing

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Zebrafish otic vesicle luminal pressure rises from 100 Pa to upwards of 300 Pa between 30 and 48 hpf (probe-based), a pressure scale of the same order of magnitude as the 65 Pa MDCK figure.
findings.evidence_quote: the pressure level gradually increases from 100 Pa to upwards of 300 Pa

findings.claim: [MEASURED] MDCK epithelial domes carry tension about 1 mN/m at small strain with a plateau at about 2 mN/m up to 300 percent areal strain (active superelasticity).
findings.evidence_quote: reached a plateau at ~2 mN/m for areal strains up to 300%

findings.claim: [MEASURED] Liver bile canaliculi: apical bulkheads act as load-bearing elements; model BC with bulkheads are twice as strong against pressure (model-inferred, not directly measured).
findings.evidence_quote: conclude that BC with bulkheads are twice as strong

findings.claim: [LIBRARY FACT] Law set 1.8.1 (lean/registry/lawsets/current.json -> lawset-1.8.1.json) pins 59 laws (verified by counting the list in the file; sha256 23c9b63e...d3). The only law applicable to lumen mechanics in it is physiology-laplace 1.0.0, status accepted, kind physical.

[LIBRARY FACT] physiology-laplace states the thin-wall wall stress P r/(2t) (sphere) and P r/t (cylinder) with an upper bound on pressure 2 sigma_max t/r. Its own assumptions: thin wall, static, no bending; no wall strength exists for any case, so it has no instance. Delphi/Constraints.lean contains no Laplace constraint wrapper (grep for laplace/Laplace there found no match).
findings.evidence_quote: For a thin-walled sphere the wall stress is P r / (2 t) and for a cylinder P r / t

findings.claim: [LIBRARY FACT, differs from earlier law-mapper] The cell-geometry candidates the earlier mapper listed (plateau-triple-junction-120, hexagon-of-120, twelve-pentagons...), the CellGeometry.lean module and the ThompsonLaws library (Cells.lean: Young-Laplace tension form, Plateau-Rayleigh, partition curvature) are ABSENT from the application repo lean/ directory at 1.8.1 (grep for tripleJunction / ThompsonLaws / CellGeometry over D:/.../delphisci/lean returned nothing). They exist only in the split-out copy D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/upstream/leanbio (CellGeometry.lean sha256 4bfbd8b2...5ac86a5969; ThompsonLaws/Cells.lean defines laplacePressure T k1 k2 = T*(k1+k2)), which is the older 1.6.0 tree. So the newer repo has FEWER lumen-relevant laws, not more; the earlier mapper's file claims are valid for the leanbio tree only.

[DERIVED, my reading] Link between data and law: the Young-Laplace form (pressure = tension x summed curvature, uniform tension, one pressure) forces constant mean curvature, so a lumen with 13-48 percent concave surface (measured) cannot be a uniform-tension single-pressure surface. This is what Vasquez et al. argue qualitatively; the formal statement (ThompsonLaws.Cells.biconcave_not_equilibrium) is in leanbio, not in law set 1.8.1, and I did not run Lean.

findings.claim: [REVIEW STATEMENT] Vertex models treat cells as 2D polygons whose vertices move under growth, interfacial tension and pressure; the virtual-work formulation defines cell pressure P, surface tension T and line tension Lambda.
findings.evidence_quote: Vertex models are a class of such models that consider cells as individual objects, approximated by two-dimensional polygons representing cellular interfaces

findings.claim: [REVIEW STATEMENT] Fluid accumulation in a lumen generates outward hydrostatic pressure capable of shaping morphogenesis from organ to body-plan scale.
findings.evidence_quote: Accumulation of fluid within a luminal space can generate outward hydrostatic pressure capable of shaping morphogenesis

findings.claim: [REVIEW STATEMENT] Tissue-hydraulics review gives order-of-magnitude estimates of physical parameters for lumen formation and coarsening (linear irreversible thermodynamics framework); abstract only, estimates not read.
findings.evidence_quote: We focus on order of magnitude estimates of physical parameters controlling lumen formation and coarsening.

key_claims.claim: In MDCK spheroids the lumen is measurably non-spherical (sphericity about 0.3-0.7) with a large concave fraction (10 to over 50 percent of surface), unlike the nearly spherical outer surface.
key_claims.evidence_quote: The sphericity of lumens ranged from Ψ ~ 0.70 to very far from spherical ( Ψ ~ 0.3)

key_claims.claim: Claudin-knockout (leaky) MDCK cysts form lumens of unchanged solidity, which Vasquez et al. take to mean pressure alone is not the main shape determinant; apical size per cell and cell number are.
key_claims.evidence_quote: We conclude that, at least in this model system, pressure alone is not the primary driver for determining lumen shape and size.

key_claims.claim: The pressure role is contested: an independent lab measures about 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and argues lumen dynamics are pressure-determined, while Vasquez et al. never measure pressure (their p is dimensionless).
key_claims.evidence_quote: Hydrostatic pressure measurements show an average of 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and close to 0 Pa in epiblasts.

key_claims.claim: Under law set 1.8.1 the only applicable accepted law is physiology-laplace (thin-wall stress/pressure bound); the cell-geometry and Thompson-library lumen theorems the earlier mapper cited are not in the 1.8.1 application repo, only in the older leanbio copy.
key_claims.evidence_quote: For a thin-walled sphere the wall stress is P r / (2 t) and for a cylinder P r / t

recommendations: Before any frozen-prediction test, first check the claim that solidity depends on genotype at matched size with the paper's 2D KS test; my simple tests do not show it for Rab11a (p=0.066 adjusted, 0.755 raw).

Treat the apical length per cell as genotype-and-size dependent: Spearman l_a vs cell number is 0.01 (WT) but -0.44 (Rab11a) and +0.61 (Cldn-qKO), so a design that assumes it is a constant of the genotype should test that first.
Treat pressure as unmeasured in the Vasquez cysts; any pascal-valued prediction must borrow 65 Pa (Lu 2025) and a tension scale, and the two available tension scales differ 10-20 x.

For the law library: under 1.8.1 only physiology-laplace is usable and it has no instance or Laplace rules-out wrapper in Constraints.lean; either re-import the CellGeometry/ThompsonLaws theorems from leanbio into the 1.8.1 tree through the normal proposal route or state that no lumen-shape law is available.
Obtain the Mukenhirn 2024 source data (pressure and tension per cyst) to replace the borrowed numbers.

could_not_find: Numeric pressures, tensions and apical-belt values from Mukenhirn 2024 Dev Cell: paywalled, and the bioRxiv preprint and Europe PMC preprint file returned 403/500. Only the abstract was read.
Numeric values in Guha Ray 2026 (PRX Life): the two-column PDF text interleaves; values are in figures, which I could not read as numbers. Table II ratio estimates were garbled and not used.
Chan 2019 (blastocyst) and Dumortier 2019 numbers: paywalled; only the "twofold pressure increase" statement from the abstract.
Torres-Sanchez 2021 order-of-magnitude parameter table: full text not accessible.
The paper's size-matched 2D Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of Rab11a and ddAVP effects: I did not run it, so the Rab11a-lowers-solidity claim is unconfirmed by my simple tests.

The 15,030-row sweep was not re-fit or re-simulated by me; the earlier design report claims the best sweep setting has solidity RMSE 0.229 vs 0.124 for a constant. I did not reproduce that, so it is cited only as an earlier-agent claim, not as a finding here.
A measurement of pressure, 3D shape and apical area in the SAME MDCK cysts: not found in any source read. Vasquez has shape without pressure; Lu has pressure without per-lumen shape tables.
Why the tension scale differs by 10-20 x between Lu 2025 model (0.1 mN/m) and Latorre 2018 domes (1-2 mN/m): not resolved.

Lean was not run (not needed; only file contents and registry JSON were read). I did not re-open ThompsonLaws theorem biconcave_not_equilibrium; its name and content come from the earlier law-mapper report; only laplacePressure (Cells.lean line 23) and tripleJunction_120 / liquidCylinder_unstable declarations were located by grep.
Lumen nucleation by hollowing vs cord hollowing in vivo (zebrafish gut, mouse kidney) and organoid-scale lumen size scaling: out of scope of the sources I could read in full.
Per-genotype dimensional pressure for the Vasquez cysts: none exists in the paper; the factor ten for Cldn-qKO is a modelling constraint.

[held-out clade] and other holdout taxa: not used anywhere, per the frozen-holdout rule. Two accepted law records in the library (Thompson chapter 2 flight laws) contain holdout wording and were deliberately not opened further.

glossary.plain: The fluid-filled hollow space inside a tube, sac or ball of cells.
A small ball of cells with a hollow centre, grown in a gel in the lab.
A line of dog kidney cells widely used to study how cells form hollow structures.
The side of a cell facing the lumen / facing the gel outside / touching its neighbours.
The push of a still fluid on its container, here measured in pascals (Pa).
A unit of pressure; about 100,000 Pa is the air pressure around us.
The pulling force along a surface that makes soap bubbles and droplets round; here milli-newtons per metre.
Pressure inside a skin equals its tension times how curved it is; for a sphere P = 2T/R.
A score from 0 to 1 for how close a 3D shape is to a perfect sphere.
Shape area divided by the area of its convex hull; below 1 means the outline has dents.
Bowed inward, like the inside of a bowl.
A computer model where each cell is a polygon whose corners move according to forces and energies.
Proteins that seal the gaps between neighbouring cells so fluid cannot leak through.
A cell protein that directs membrane delivery to the lumen-facing side; overproducing it enlarges that side.
A cell line in which a gene has been deleted.
Drugs that increase / decrease the cells' pumping of fluid into the lumen.
A jelly-like gel that cells are embedded in to grow in 3D.
